threadParts:
Threadplane 0.1.0 is out.

Chat, durable threads, human approvals, subagents, and generative UI for Angular — on LangGraph or AG-UI.

All of it MIT. No paid tier, no account, no activation.

But the version number is the honest part 🧵

Through 0.0.66 we only ever bumped the patch digit.

55 commits of breaking changes went out under a counter that said nothing had broken.

That's not semver. That's a lie with a decimal point in it.

0.1.0 is the release where the number starts telling the truth.

What's actually finished is the last mile — everything between "my agent streams tokens" and "my team can put this in front of a customer."

That gap is where Angular teams lose weeks. It's the only thing this project has tried to close.

In the box:

• <chat> + 15 documented components
• durable threads, checkpoints, time travel
• interrupts and approvals
• client tools
• generative UI (json-render + A2UI)
• subagents
• 5 classified error kinds with retry
• tests that run with no model and no API key

The adapter is not a one-way door.

LangGraph and AG-UI produce the same Agent contract, so components don't know which backend they're talking to.

We tested AG-UI against AWS Strands, Microsoft Agent Framework, and Mastra. Two languages, no adapter changes.

The part I like more than the feature list is where it stops.

Your proxy. Your keys. Your CORS. Your thread IDs. You compose the interrupt panel.

Every one of those is a place where doing it for you would mean deciding it for you.

And the money, plainly: there's no open-core split.

Nothing is held back for a paid tier. The paid offerings sell review time and a response commitment — not code you can't otherwise have.

If you disagree with a decision I made, the license already grants you a fork.

Full write-up:
https://threadplane.ai/blog/threadplane-0-1-0?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=threadplane-0-1-0

Or skip me entirely and try it without a backend:

npm i @threadplane/chat @threadplane/langgraph
